text:
Score fusion needs comparable scales: OpenSearch documents per-query z-score normalization, `(s−mean)/std`, before weighted combination. [Official documentation](https://docs.opensearch.org/latest/search-plugins/search-pipelines/normalization-processor/). Mathematical implication for neural–Markov fusion: pooled global variance includes variation in prefix-specific score offsets, although those offsets cannot affect within-prefix ranking. Estimate a fixed scale from validation within-query centered residuals to avoid this confounding while keeping scores independent of candidate batches. Per-query normalization is another option, but its scale changes between 100-candidate evaluation and full-catalog recommendation. For zero variance, use a zero normalized contribution; near-zero variance needs a scale floor to avoid amplifying noise. These are implementation deductions, not established performance guarantees.

Uniform smoothing gives sparse transitions finite log probabilities. With counts `c(h,i)`, row total `C(h)`, catalog size `V`, and total pseudocount `α>0`, use `p(i|h)=(c(h,i)+α/V)/(C(h)+α)`. This is interpolation with a uniform background, consistent with established [smoothing formulations](https://www.sigir.hosting.acm.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/p268.pdf). Algebraically, `log p=log(α/V)−log(C+α)+log1p(V*c/α)`. The first two terms are constant across candidates for a fixed prefix, so ranking fusion can use only the sparse `log1p` correction. Unobserved transitions contribute zero; an empty row contributes zero everywhere. Store sparse counts and row totals, look up only requested candidate pairs, and avoid allocating full-catalog probability vectors. Preserve the constant terms when actual probabilities are required; nonuniform background smoothing requires retaining its item-dependent contribution.
